question: Which reaction is an example of a double displacement reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is '**Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) → BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In a** double displacement process**, the **positive and negative ions of two ionic compounds exchange positions to generate two new compounds**.
 
• Covalent or ionic bonds may be present between the reacting species.
 
• The **double displacement reactions** often cause the **precipitation of a single product**.
 
• The **general form** of a double displacement reaction can be given as, **AB + CD → AD + CB**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• A chemical reaction in which **one element in a compound is replaced by another** is referred to as a** single displacement reaction**. This reaction is also referred to as a **single replacement reaction or exchange reaction**.
 
• The** general form of a single displacement reaction **can be given as, A + BC → AC + B.
 
• In a chemical reaction known as a **neutralisation**, **an acid and a base combine to produce salt and water.** The **pH of the interacting acids and bases affects the pH of the salt** that forms.
